story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Blues (6-6-1) beat Boston 4-1 on Thursday. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 16th).

The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .588, and their finishing has held them back. The Rangers’ record (.536) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blues keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd), but have struggled on the power play (31st). On the other side, the Rangers get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd), lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Rangers’ power play against the Blues’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Beyond that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Dylan Holloway (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 13 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (7 G / 2 A / 9 P in 13 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL.
Joel Hofer (5-3-1 / .923 SV% in 9 GS) has been terrific for St. Louis and will likely start. Dylan Garand (4-5-1 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) is in line to start for the Rangers.
